item.text: The change path has two quota checks, and the code uses both a subscription plan and an organization plan in different places. I’m checking how those values are kept in sync and which downstream effects actually follow from the change.

item.text:
The billing page’s `selectPlan` flow in [page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx) calls `changePlanAction` with the organization ID, selected plan and a monthly interval. In [change-plan.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts), the `withAction` wrapper validates that input with `changePlanSchema`, resolves the authenticated actor for the organization and converts errors into an `ActionResult`.

`changePlanAction` first calls `can` for `org:manage_billing`. In [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/lib/permissions.ts), that permission requires an owner. Platform staff can also pass the permission check, but the cross-tenant check runs first: the actor must be scoped to the target organization. The service repeats the scope and permission checks through `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan`.

Before writing, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage` compares the target plan’s seat, project and storage limits against the organization’s usage counters. `getUsage` reads cached `organization_usage` values via [usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts); it does not recount source rows at this point. `wouldExceedLimit` in [plan-limits.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/config/plan-limits.ts) checks `used + 0 > target limit`, so usage equal to the limit is accepted and usage above it produces a `PlanLimitError`.

Then `changePlan` in [billing-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/server/services/billing-service.ts) reads the current plan and repeats the target-plan comparison for seats, projects, storage **and webhook endpoint count**. These checks run for plan changes generally, not only when the target is smaller. The change does not check issues per project or API requests before accepting the target plan.

On success, `updateSubscriptionPlan` in [subscription-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts) updates the subscription row’s `plan`, `interval`, `status` to `active`, and timestamp. Thus a deliberate change also ends a trial. `billing-service.ts`’s `planFor` treats **`subscriptions.plan` as authoritative**, falling back to `organizations.plan` only when there is no subscription.

There is an important implementation consequence: `updateSubscriptionPlan` does **not** update the separate `organizations.plan` value. After the write, `changePlan` emits `billing.plan_changed` with the old and new subscription plans. Registered listeners in [activity-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/server/services/activity-service.ts) record a plan-change activity, and [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) queues deliveries for enabled endpoints subscribed to that event. `emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for listeners to settle but does not fail the change when a listener throws. Finally, the action revalidates the organization and billing cache tags.

Away from billing, the new subscription value reaches `checkLimit` in `billing-service.ts`. For example, the dashboard [layout.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx) obtains seat and project checks from it, as does the members settings page for seats. Their checks can therefore reflect the smaller subscription allowance.

Many other product paths instead read **`organizations.plan`**, so this particular change leaves them using the old plan. These include invitation, project, issue, attachment and webhook creation guards in their respective services; flag evaluation through `buildFlagContext` and `isEnabled`; advanced search, CSV export and digest eligibility; webhook delivery; and the retention window in `runCleanupArchivedJob`. The dashboard’s flag snapshot likewise uses the organization value. Consequently, those paths do not necessarily start enforcing the smaller plan when this action succeeds. The plan-aware limiter in [rate-limit.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/f79692d3-f8eb-432c-9d75-7a4c06ab1c79/src/lib/rate-limit.ts) has a `setOrgPlan` function, but the change path does not call it, so the change does not propagate there either.
